chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa al-Daqqaq narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Qadi al-Alawi al-Abbasi narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Nasir (may God sanctify his spirit) narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Rashid narrated to me, from his uncle Abu Ma'mar Sa'id ibn Khuthaym, from his brother Mu'ammar, who said:

I was sitting with al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) when Zayd ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) came and held onto the two doorposts. Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said to him: "O uncle, I seek refuge in God for you from being the one crucified at Kinasa." The mother of Zayd said to him: "By God, nothing drives you to say this except envy of my son." He (peace be upon him) said: "If only it were envy, if only it were envy" -- three times. Then he said: "My father narrated to me, from my grandfather (peace be upon them both), that from his progeny there will emerge a man named Zayd, who will be killed in Kufa and crucified at Kinasa. He will be exhumed from his grave. The gates of heaven will be opened for his spirit, and the inhabitants of the heavens will rejoice in him. His spirit will be placed in the crop of a green bird that roams wherever it wishes in Paradise."

key_terms.الكناسة: Kinasa -- a marketplace/district in Kufa where Zayd's body was displayed
key_terms.المصلوب: The crucified one -- referring to the prophesied crucifixion of Zayd ibn Ali
key_terms.حوصلة طير أخضر: The crop of a green bird -- an Islamic motif indicating the honored status of martyrs in Paradise

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the martyrdom of Zayd ibn Ali?
ai.summary: This narration describes a poignant encounter where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) warned his uncle Zayd ibn Ali about his future martyrdom and crucifixion at Kinasa (a district of Kufa), based on a prophecy transmitted from Imam al-Husayn (AS). When Zayd's mother accused the Imam of envy, he expressed sorrow and revealed that Zayd's spirit would be honored in Paradise within a green bird -- a motif found in hadith literature about martyrs. Zayd ibn Ali's revolt against the Umayyad governor in 122 AH and his subsequent crucifixion are historically documented events.

en.bilal-muhammad: `Ali b. Ahmad b. Musa al-Daqqaq narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. al-Husayn al-Qadi al-`Alawi al-`Abbasi narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan b. `Ali al-Nasir (qr) narrated to me. He said: Ahmad b. Rashid narrated to me from his uncle Abi Mu`ammar Sa`id b. Kathim from his brother Mu`ammar.

He said: I was sitting with al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as) when Zayd b. `Ali b. al-Husayn (as) came and held onto the peg of the door. So, al-Sadiq (as) said to him: O uncle! I seek refuge in Allah for you being crucified in Kinasa. So, the mother of Zayd said to him: By Allah, nothing caused you to say this except for envy for my son. So, he (as) said: I wish it were envy, I wish it were envy – three times.  Then, he said: My father narrated to me from my grandfather (as) that he would have a descendant named “Zayd”, who will be killed in Kufa, crucified in Kinasa, and resurrected from his grave. The gates of heaven will be opened for his spirit, and the people of heaven will be rejoiced by him. His spirit will be put in the stomach of a green bird, which will wander wherever it wishes in Paradise.
